edges.why: The theory lessons in The Science of Consciousness assume the vocabulary and the care about evidence introduced in Introduction to Consciousness.
Comparing human and machine intelligence is easier once you know how AI systems learn and are evaluated.
The comparison also uses ideas about experience, awareness and understanding from Introduction to Consciousness.
Philosophy of Mind builds on the question of what experience is.
Philosophical positions frame what the scientific theories are trying to explain.
The two foundational courses are independent and meet in the lessons on machine consciousness.
Brain and cognition background supports the neuroscience lessons in Introduction to Consciousness.
AI ethics is easier to follow when you know what AI systems can and cannot do.
Artificial memory systems connect memory and identity to machine intelligence.

compass.intro: The Learning Compass suggests where to begin. It does not measure ability or personality, and your answers stay in your browser. You can skip it at any time.

questions.text: How familiar are you with how artificial intelligence works?
How familiar are you with neuroscience and the brain?
How interested are you in philosophy?
How comfortable are you reading how a scientific study works?
How deep would you like to go?
What do you most want to understand?
